features.title: Everything a SaaS needs on day one
features.description: The product surface is already built, so you can spend your time on what makes yours different.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.description: Email or Google sign-in, email verification, and password reset.

organizations.title: Organizations
organizations.description: Invite members by email and give each one a role.

admin.title: Admin panel
admin.description: Manage users, bans, and platform roles in one place.

storage.title: File uploads
storage.description: Avatars and logos on any S3-compatible bucket with dimah-s3.

i18n.title: i18n and RTL
i18n.description: English and Persian out of the box, with right-to-left layouts.

serverFirst.title: Server-first
serverFirst.description: Session in Server Components, cached reads, and a Server Action for every write.

nextjs.eyebrow: Next.js 16, the way it is meant to be used
nextjs.title: Built on Cache Components
nextjs.description: Pages open on an instant static shell and stream in the signed-in parts. Data stays cached until someone changes it, and then the change shows at once.

prefetch.title: Instant navigation
prefetch.description: Partial Prefetching loads each page's shell ahead of the click; only the parts that need your session wait for the server.

cache.title: Cached reads, tagged
cache.description: Lists are 'use cache' functions tagged per user or organization, so a visit does not mean a database query.

update.title: Fresh right after a write
update.description: A Server Action calls updateTag, and the person who made the change sees it in the same response, with no refetch or client cache.

secure.title: Checks next to the data
secure.description: Every data read checks permissions itself, not only the layout, and sessions are never cached.

faq.description: What to expect before you build your product on Dimah Starter.

free.question: Is it free for commercial use?
free.answer: Yes. It is MIT licensed: use it for client work or your own SaaS. Keep the license notice in copies of the code; nothing else is required.

serverFirst.question: Why no client-side data library?
serverFirst.answer: Server Components and Server Actions already cover reads and writes, and keep sessions, permissions, and database access on the server. The browser loads less JavaScript, and there is one source of truth.

deploy.question: Where can I deploy it?
deploy.answer: Anywhere that runs Next.js on Node.js: Vercel, a container, or your own server. On serverless, use a pooled PostgreSQL connection. The README has a production checklist.

customize.question: Do I have to keep Persian or multi-tenancy?
customize.answer: No. Remove a locale or a dashboard area by deleting its folder and its messages; the guides list the steps. Layouts stay correct for left-to-right and right-to-left either way.

aiAgents.question: Does it work with AI coding agents?
aiAgents.answer: Yes. AGENTS.md, task guides, and Cursor rules tell Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex where each kind of code goes and which existing feature to copy.

missing.question: What is not included?
missing.answer: Billing, a CMS, and analytics are left to you, so you can choose the provider that fits your product.
